context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

lua_executor_finding_resolution.conclusion: Confirmed genuine host-load timing flake, unrelated to this branch. `git diff --stat main...HEAD -- lib/ test/` shows this branch touches only lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md, lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs, test/specs/REQ-218.md -- zero overlap with lib/letflow/engine/lua/ or its test, independently re-confirmed here (not merely re-read from TEST-RUNNER's report). Ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs` in isolation 5 consecutive times in the foreground (own shell, own PIDs): all 5 runs printed `Result: 45 passed, 11 excluded`, 5/5 passed, 0 failures. This test also appeared (and passed with no failure entry) in this session's own independent scripts/test_parallel.sh run (partition 4) and in this session's own independent mix letflow.check.test run. The AC-1 assertion (small_elapsed_ms < large_elapsed_ms, a hard wall-clock ordering between two elapsed-time measurements) is inherently susceptible to scheduler jitter under the heavy host load a ~27-minute full-suite single-process run produces; under isolated/lighter load it is stable. Classified as (a) known timing-sensitive flake, not a regression connected to REQ-218 or any of this session's changes.

ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.source_of_truth: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-218 entry, read directly (lines ~12867 onward), not paraphrased from any prior handoff.
ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.AC1: Confirmed via direct read of poller_test.exs:479-507 (describe "REQ-218 AC1..."). Test holds a probe try_acquire(:global) before a tick with pool_size:3/reserved_headroom:2 (global_cap effectively exhausted), asserts all 3 schemas' due timers stay 'pending' after that tick, then releases the probe and asserts all 3 flip to 'fired' on the next tick, and the GenServer's handle_info/2 returns {:noreply, ...} (no crash) in both cases. Satisfied.
ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.AC2: Confirmed via direct read of poller_test.exs:509-527 (describe "REQ-218 AC2..."). global_cap effectively 1 (pool_size:3/reserved_headroom:2), no probe held, all 3 schemas' due timers assert 'fired' after one single handle_info(:tick, ...) call -- proves sequential acquire/release drains all 3 within one tick, not a permanent block. Satisfied.
ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.AC3: Two independently-verified sub-clauses, both present in poller_test.exs: (a) lines 570-602, a capacity rejection for one schema's poll_and_fire does not block a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation later in the tick; (b) lines 684-728 (the newly-added per-schema clause test), a rejection for a schema's poll_and_fire does not block that SAME schema's OTHER operations (retention sweep) later in the same tick. Both read directly and confirmed non-vacuous. Satisfied.
ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.AC4: Confirmed via direct read of poller_test.exs:734-742 and lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex directly: `refute source =~ "{:tenant,"` against File.read!/1 of poller.ex's real source is a live, automated ExUnit assertion (not an informal grep). Independently grepped lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex myself for `{:tenant` -- zero occurrences (grep exit 1). All 6 with_admission/3 call sites (poller.ex handle_info/2 plus the five maybe_run_* functions) pass only `:global`. Satisfied.
ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.AC5: Confirmed via direct read of poller.ex's with_admission/3 (lines ~150-172): the acquire/release is `case Admission.try_acquire(:global) do {:ok, ref} -> try do fun.() after Admission.release(ref) end; {:error, :capacity} -> Logger.warning(...) end`, so the `after` clause is the sole release path regardless of any inner rescue. poller_test.exs:744-772 (describe "REQ-218 AC5...") forces a genuine raise through an existing per-operation rescue path and asserts the tick does not crash, a different intact schema's own timer still fires, and a post-tick probe try_acquire(:global) still succeeds under a constrained cap (proving no ref leak). Satisfied.
ac_by_ac_reconfirmation.AC6: mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test both independently re-run and passed in this session (see own_independent_test_parallel_run and own_independent_check_test_run above; both are supersets of a plain `mix test`/`mix compile --warnings-as-errors` pass with zero warnings and zero REQ-218-related failures). Satisfied with real output quoted above.

result.summary: PASS. Independently resolved TEST-RUNNER's flagged Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest finding as a genuine host-load timing flake (5/5 isolated passes, zero diff overlap with lib/letflow/engine/lua/, passed cleanly in both of this session's own full-suite runs). Per this project's structural (not count-matching) failure-attribution rule, my own run surfaced a DIFFERENT third failure than TEST-RUNNER's run did, and both were independently traced to zero code overlap with this branch. Re-derived and confirmed all 6 of REQ-218's acceptance criteria directly against the current lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex and test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs source -- all satisfied, non-vacuously. Zero {:tenant, occurrences in poller.ex (AC4), zero ISS-0069 regression signature in either full-suite run, zero PollerTest failures anywhere. requirement_status confirmed accurate (in_progress, only a started event, no stale done/verified). No decision-record contradiction found (docs/migration/decisions/ has no REQ-218/admission entries to contradict). Not a stage-gate run, so no stage-doc REVIEWER sign-off check applies.
